expectations.text: Flags that the runbook never states who it is for or what the reader already knows
expectations.evidence: C1/C2/C3: 'no sentence names the reader, what they already know, the problem the runbook solves, or what it leaves out', with an audience frontmatter rewrite.

expectations.text: Flags that the rollback procedure, the thing a reader of a runbook needs, is not at the top and is split across two sections
expectations.evidence: C4/C6: 'The rollback command first appears in the third section... Rewrite: open with the procedure.' S7/S5: 'the one procedure is split across two sections with nearly the same heading.'

expectations.text: Flags that the heading 'Rollback is automatic' contradicts its body, which describes a manual kubectl command
expectations.evidence: S2: 'the body describes a manual rollback, so the first sentence breaks the heading's promise.'

expectations.text: Flags that the processor timeout is stated as 30 seconds in one place and 60 seconds in others
expectations.evidence: S6/S5: 'Architecture says "it times out after 30 seconds"; the config example sets processor_timeout_seconds: 60; Notes says ... 60 seconds.'

expectations.text: Flags that worker, consumer and job runner name the same component, or asks whether they are one component
expectations.evidence: L5: 'The reader cannot tell whether these are one process or three'.

expectations.text: Flags at least one pronoun ('it') whose antecedent is ambiguous
expectations.evidence: 'L1, 2: "it times out" (the processor or the consumer?), "It should recover" (the deployment or the charge success rate?).'

expectations.text: Flags the 'in the YAML file, not in the Helm chart' contrast as unexplained or as implying an unstated rule
expectations.evidence: E1/E2: 'The "not in the Helm chart" contrast is useful only if the reader is told what happens when they set it there.'

expectations.text: Flags writer-serving content: the 'This section will discuss' opener, the migration history, or 'It's worth noting'
expectations.evidence: C4/C6 'drop the history from the runbook entirely'; 'L13, 2: "This section will discuss", "It's worth noting that".'

expectations.text: Orders findings with reader/contract problems before structure problems before sentence-level problems
expectations.evidence: Sections in order: '## Contract', '## Structure', '## Local'.

expectations.text: Gives a concrete rewrite for most findings, not only a description of the problem
expectations.evidence: Each of the 8 main findings has a 'Rewrite:' line, most with concrete text (frontmatter block, numbered rollback steps, '## Roll back', 'Set the retry count in `config/payments.yaml`...'). Only the four 'smaller' bullets lack rewrites.
